answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity with refundable bonds: every agent locks a deposit that is slashed only when peers attest to fake identities, so creating thousands of sybils becomes expensive instead of free. Like a ripple spreading through a reputation graph, each verified attestation strengthens the bond between real agents, while a relic of past fraud - a public, signed record of slashed deposits - lets newcomers check history before trusting. As the tide of new agents rises, the bond requirement scales with demand, keeping entry open for honest agents, costly for attackers.
